outcome: The general conjecture (existence of a universal constant t0 such that every t0-tough graph is Hamiltonian) remains fully open; no new upper or lower bound on t0 itself has been reported since 26 January 2024. All post-2024 activity settles Hamiltonicity only for restricted, forbidden-subgraph graph classes, or a separate degree-sequence conjecture of Hoàng, neither of which is a case of the stated existence question.
summary: Chvátal's toughness conjecture (1973) posits a universal constant t0 such that every t0-tough graph on ≥3 vertices is Hamiltonian. The known bracket — t0 must be at least 9/4 (Bauer, Broersma & Veldman 2000) if it exists — long predates the window and is unchanged. I searched arXiv, the current Wikipedia 'Graph toughness' article, and general web/scholar-style queries for any 2024–2026 movement on the existential question itself and found none: no new lower bound (a t-tough non-Hamiltonian graph for larger t), no new upper bound (a proof that some specific t0 works in general), and no disproof of the conjecture's existence. What I did find is a steady stream of 2024–2026 papers proving Hamiltonicity for graphs that are t-tough AND belong to some forbidden-induced-subgraph class (e.g. arXiv:2503.12860 'every 2k-connected (P2∪kP1)-free graph...', arXiv:2504.08936 on (P4∪P1)-free graphs, arXiv:2505.04189 on 15-tough (P3∪3P1)-free graphs, arXiv:2506.12684 on 11-tough (2P2∪P1)-free graphs, and its successor arXiv:2608.24047 improving the same class's toughness bound from 11 to 10, and arXiv:2605.19508 on 1-tough (P2∪kP1)-free graphs). These are results about a different (restricted, forbidden-subgraph) family of graphs, not a case obtained by narrowing a parameter of the stated conjecture — under §3.1 they are 'related problems' (variants), not cases, because the original conjecture quantifies over ALL graphs and forbidding an induced subgraph changes the object class rather than restricting within it in a way that would, if resolved for all classes, sum to the general conjecture. I also found arXiv:2503.14735 (Shan and, per one summary, Tanyel) verifying Hoàng's 1995 conjecture (a distinct, stronger degree-sequence statement) for all t≥4 — again a different conjecture that happens to imply Chvátal's classical 1972 degree-condition theorem as a special case, not the toughness conjecture itself. I found no AI involvement anywhere in this line of work: none of the papers I opened (2503.14735, 2506.12684, 2503.12860, 2608.24047) mention AI, machine learning, or computer-assisted proof of any kind — these are conventional human combinatorial proofs. A search for AI/LLM connections to this specific conjecture (including checking Terence Tao's and the Erdős-problems AI-tracking material for any overlap) turned up nothing relating to toughness/Hamiltonicity. The triage's `found` list was empty but its `why` cited arXiv:2608.24047, which I confirmed exists (a real September 2026 preprint improving the (2P2∪P1)-free toughness bound from 11 to 10) — the triage's characterization of it was accurate even though the item wasn't logged in `found`.
competing_reading: One could argue forbidding an induced linear forest F is 'restricting attention to' the graphs in that class, which resembles a case rather than a variant, since Wikipedia's own general-topic articles sometimes list such F-free results as 'progress toward' the toughness conjecture. But settling Hamiltonicity for, say, 10-tough (2P2∪P1)-free graphs says nothing about whether some fixed t0 works for ALL graphs — a graph outside that forbidden class at toughness 10 could still be non-Hamiltonian, so this is not territory removed from the universally-quantified existence question in the way a dimension-restricted case would be for, say, a conjecture indexed by dimension. I classify these as variants (open, no_change_found) rather than partial results, but flag the line as genuinely fuzzy given how survey literature (e.g. Bauer–Broersma–Schmeichel) frames these graph-class results as 'the conjecture verified for X'.
what_would_settle_it: A paper either exhibiting, for every ε>0, a non-Hamiltonian graph with toughness t0-ε for arbitrarily large claimed t0 (refuting the conjecture), or proving Hamiltonicity for all sufficiently tough graphs with no forbidden-subgraph restriction (proving it) would settle the general question. Absent that, the next-most-informative event would be a change to the known lower bound of 9/4 for what t0 must be, which also has not occurred since 2024.
